# \textcolor{mybgcolor2}{Highlights}

\vspace*{-5truemm}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=pale_blue, colframe=mybgcolor4, boxsep=3pt, left=4pt]
\color{mybgcolor4}
\large

\begin{itemize}[itemsep=0.8em, topsep=0.5em, leftmargin=*] 
    \item \underline{\textbf{Published a fully validated qPCR eDNA assay for sunflower stars}} \normalsize (\textit{Pycnopodia helianthoides}), spawning a slough of new and ongoing research partnerships and funding to identify remnant populations in California, understand the drivers of eDNA fate and transport, and to benchmark quantitative abundance estimation.
    \item \large \underline{\textbf{Maintained our high throughput lab processing,}} \normalsize including sample collection, extractions, sequencing, and qPCR, increasing our ability to generate ocean biomolecular observations.
    \item \large \underline{\textbf{Advanced our biomolecular data management workflows}}, \normalsize developing a robust laboratory information management system that records data from sample collection to data provisioning. This included publishing \underline{\textbf{2 peer reviewed manuscripts}} and publishing \underline{\textbf{35 SOPS}} (BeBOP FAIRe protocols).
\end{itemize}

\end{tcolorbox}

## Cruises

\vspace*{-3truemm}

```{r cruises}

# Create pretty version of table that will go into report
cruises <- gsheet2tbl("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18LKb5Foy-P0oiZI6J8-HJ7tYcr-nMh9tYHbOaEGHHJQ/edit?gid=1815279931#gid=1815279931") %>% 
  filter(., Year=="FY26")

header <- "2026 Cruises"
footnote<-"OME executed fieldwork on 9 cruises in 2026."
nickname <- "Cruise_table" # this is so you can refer to it later systematically
alttext <- "This is a 5-column table of Year,	Cruise,Name,	Region,	Project, and	OME Participant. "
# Create data-saver version of table that will be used to reference things later saved as backup
table_raw<-cruises
# Create pretty version of table that will go into report
table_print <- table_raw

```


We participated in \underline{\textbf{`r xunits(nrow(table_raw))`}} cruises in `r paste0(table_raw[[1,1]])`. 

```{r, out.width="95%", background='white'}

```

## Sample Collection and Processing

\vspace*{-3truemm}

```{r scp}
library(gsheet)
dat <- gsheet2tbl('https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18LKb5Foy-P0oiZI6J8-HJ7tYcr-nMh9tYHbOaEGHHJQ/edit?gid=342601147#gid=342601147')

dat %>%
mutate(., `Sequenced:Count`=as.character(`Sequenced:Count`)) %>% 
mutate(., `Sequenced:Markers`=as.character(`Sequenced:Markers`)) %>% 
mutate(., `qPCR:Count`=as.character(`qPCR:Count`)) %>% 
mutate(Index = (row_number())) %>%
pivot_longer(cols = c(contains(':')),
names_to = c("Process"),
values_to = c("Value")) %>%
separate(Process, c("Process", "Kind") ) %>%
mutate(Index_2 = str_c(Process, Index)) %>%
filter(., !is.na(Value)) %>%
pivot_wider(names_from =Kind, values_from = Value, values_fill = NA) %>%
filter(., Year !="Previous") %>%
filter(., Count !="Previous") %>%
mutate(., Count=as.numeric(Count)) %>% 
mutate(., Markers=as.numeric(Markers)) %>% 
mutate(., Total=Count*Markers) %>% 
mutate(., Count = if_else(Process=="Sequenced", Total, Count)) -> dat_c

# dat_c %>%
#   group_by(Process, Year) %>% 
#   dplyr::summarise(Count=sum(Count))
```

```{r scp_plot, fig.height=2.6, fig.width=10, out.width="95%", fig.align="center"}
header <- "Sample Collection and Processing"
footnote<-c("Data switched from civilian to Federal in 2023.")
nickname <- "scp_plot"
alttext <- "This is a bar plot of sample collection and processing numbers."
  
# Select data and make plot
figure <- dat_c %>%
  group_by(Process, Year) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(Count=sum(Count)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = Count, fill = Process)) +
  geom_bar(position="dodge", stat="identity") +
  facet_wrap(~Process, scales="free_y", nrow=1) +
  theme_pubr() +
  theme(strip.background= element_rect(fill = '#001743'),
        strip.text = element_text(colour = 'white'),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1, vjust = 1), 
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = 'white', colour = '#001743'),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = 'white', colour = '#001743'),
        axis.line = element_line(colour = '#001743'),
        text = element_text(color = "#001743"),
        axis.title = element_text(colour = "#001743", face = "bold"),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = "#001743")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c(natparks.pals("Saguaro", 5)[1],
                             natparks.pals("Saguaro", 5)[2],
                             natparks.pals("Saguaro", 5)[3],
                             natparks.pals("Saguaro", 5)[4]))

figure
```

\vspace*{-3truemm}

**Figure 1.** OME has continued to maintain efficiency and execute sample collection and processing.
